newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. Security Council maintains sanctions on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Security Council maintains sanctions on Iraq.

text.p: The U.N. Security Council on Monday retained intact the stiff economic sanctions imposed on Baghdad since its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The expected decision, relayed by diplomats, was made during a review of the sanctions conducted every 60 days.
A prime condition for any lifting of the embargoes is a clean bill of health from the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) in charge of scrapping Iraq's weapons of mass destruction.

UNSCOM chief Rolf Ekeus, who briefed the council on a recent trip to Baghdad, is still not satisfied Iraq has made full disclosure in the areas of long-range missiles, chemical and biological programs and related documents.
Since discovering a cache of documents in the summer of 1995, Ekeus has feared that nerve gas and dangerous chemical weapons are still hidden in Iraq.

In recent months U.N. inspectors found evidence engineers were conducting research work related to the development of banned long-range ballistic missiles, including a software package on Iraqi computers apparently obtained after the 1991 Gulf War. But officials say they do not know if this is a model or that Iraq is actually constructing such missiles.

Iraq, however, recently did allow the inspectors to export some missile engine parts dug up in the Iraqi desert so they can be analyzed by U.S. experts in Huntsville, Ala. The purpose is to determine whether the engines were taken from some of the missiles not accounted for earlier.
